| w3-dns-publish follow-up 9 | F10-03 measured on the pinned AdGuard Home v0.107.59 through the real node/dns Apply on two owned resolvers (36 per-query traces + the complete authority history): ordinary primary hits keep the TTL-10 data with per-second decrement and no authority exchange, fresh fetch after 10.1 s; the secondary caches independently; whole-second expiry permits a same-primary fresh answer at 9.35 s (precision, not optimistic caching); a delayed first fetch of 2,502 ms caches normally, one dropped upstream packet 10,001 ms then retry success, two drops SERVFAIL at 20,001 ms, controlled client fallback 2,501 ms — latency alone does not select the cause; **F9-INFLIGHT**: a late upstream reply arriving after the client abandons the request but before AdGuard's 10 s timeout replaces a newer cache entry (new→old within 1.3 s; inherent insertion ordering, no exposed cache / mode / timeout setting fixes it; TTL is a maximum lifetime, not a minimum retention or cross-query consistency guarantee); defaults read back live after Apply (cache_size 4194304, cache_ttl_min/max 0/0, cache_optimistic false, upstream_timeout 10 s, fallback_dns []); BACKEND §2.1.5 + row F9-CACHE with the fetch-vs-fallback / outstanding-request attribution rule; dns-positive-cache conformance target + mandatory DNS PR gate (a future pin that changes the behaviour fails); the historical members F10-03 run 2be2d32f stays failed and unattributed; production blocked_response_ttl still 待決策; requests to devstack (dns_trace outstanding-request correlation) and members (AT20 attribution) | done (#345) |
